topic: The Pi Collision Mystery: How Colliding Blocks Calculate the Universe's Most Famous Constant
target_audience: Undergraduate Physics/Math students or Advanced High School Students

sections.title: The Hook: The Counting Machine
lecture_lines: Imagine two blocks on a frictionless floor.
They collide with a wall and each other.
For specific mass ratios, collisions reveal Pi.
animations: Draw a horizontal line #FFFFFF (floor) and a vertical line #FFFFFF (wall) at the left. Place a small red #FF0000 square (mass m) and a large blue #0000FF square (mass M) on the floor.
The blue square moves left at a constant velocity. Above them, display 'Collisions: 0' in light gray #D3D3D3.
Animate the squares bouncing between each other and the wall. The counter increments on each impact. Stop when the blue square moves right, with counter at 31.

sections.title: Prerequisite Knowledge: Conservation Laws
lecture_lines: Conservation of energy and momentum drive this system.
Energy creates an elliptical boundary for velocities.
These laws constrain every possible bounce.
animations: Display the formulas 'Kinetic Energy: $1/2mv^2$' and 'Momentum: $mv$' in yellow #FFFF00 at the top of the screen.
Draw a coordinate system with axes v1 and v2. Render a blue #0000FF ellipse centered at the origin representing the energy conservation equation.
Show a dot on the ellipse. When a collision occurs, animate the dot moving to a new position on the ellipse along a straight line (chord).

sections.title: Geometric Transformation: From Ellipse to Circle
lecture_lines: Kinetic energy conservation defines an elliptical velocity boundary.
Scaling the velocity morphs the ellipse into a circle.
This circular geometry simplifies the system's complex dynamics.
animations: Start with the blue #0000FF ellipse on the v1, v2 plane. Label the axes.
Apply a vertical scaling transformation to the entire plane by a factor of sqrt(M/m). The ellipse morphs into a green #00FF00 circle.
Display the equation $v_1^2 + (sqrt(M/m)v_2)^2 = C$ which simplifies to $x^2 + y^2 = R^2$ in white #FFFFFF.

sections.title: The Physics of a Bounce: A Reflection in State Space
lecture_lines: A dot on the circle represents the system's state.
Every physical collision reflects the point across the circle.
Successive bounces create a zigzag path of state transitions.
animations: Draw the green #00FF00 circle. Place a bright white #FFFFFF dot on the circumference to represent the initial state.
Show a reflection: the dot moves along a straight line (chord) to a new point on the circle, representing one collision.
Repeat this reflection 5 times rapidly, leaving a trace of the path to show a zigzag pattern inside the circle.

sections.title: Connecting to Pi: The Arc Length
lecture_lines: Increasing mass ratio makes the reflection angle tiny.
Collisions map out the circle's arc length.
Reversing direction requires traversing the full arc.
Total reflections equal Pi divided by the angle.
This count exactly matches the digits of Pi.
animations: In the green #00FF00 circle, label the arc between two collision points as an angle theta in cyan #00FFFF.
Show the formula theta approx sqrt(m/M) in white #FFFFFF. Explain that for large M, theta is very small.
Animate the dot moving in small steps around the circle. Highlight the semi-circle arc, representing pi radians of total phase change.
Show a calculation: Number of collisions N = pi / theta. For M=100^2, N = 314.
Highlight the first three digits of the collision count (3, 1, 4) in gold #FFD700 as they appear.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Power of Phase Space
lecture_lines: Phase space reveals hidden constants in nature.
Pi emerges from the symmetry of conservation.
Abstract geometry solves deep physical mysteries.
animations: Display a split view. Left side shows the [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/blocks.svg] and wall; right side shows the state point moving on the circle.
Animate a full sequence for M=100^3. The collision counter on the left and the arc on the right both finish at 3141.
Clear the screen and display the text 'The geometry of phase space reveals pi' in gold #FFD700.
